title: AGC Collective Actions Limited v. Alphabet Inc., Google LLC, Google Ireland Limited and Google UK Limited
primaryStatutes: Article 102 TFEU for the applicable pre-Brexit period

plaintiffs: AGC Collective Actions Limited as proposed class representative

summary: AGC seeks authorization to bring collective damages claims alleging abuse of dominance in digital-advertising markets. The proceeding remains at the certification stage; no class has been certified and no liability has been established.
coreQuestion: Is AGC a suitable class representative, are the claims eligible for collective treatment, and do the pleaded ad-tech practices plausibly constitute abuse of dominance?

applicant: Google's alleged market practices caused economic loss to proposed class members.
respondents: Consult CAT filings for certification and merits responses.

timeline.event: Application received by the Competition Appeal Tribunal.
Summary of Collective Proceedings Claim Form published.

analysis.importance: Tracks collective competition litigation over ad-tech platform control.
uncertainties: The claim should not be labeled a fabricated-click case absent pleaded support.

logisticsTranslation.disruptions: funding challenges, class narrowing, or certification refusal
logisticsTranslation.decisionLesson: Control of a routing layer can create systemwide pricing and access effects.

disclaimer: Allegations are unproven and certification is pending. CAT documents control.
